merged.title: fix(port): Vulkan pipeline parts take only their own state; bindings only their own stages
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
#216's pipeline-library linking built each shared part with the whole state of the first key that needed it. NVIDIA (GTX 1070, 580.178) carried the vertex input given to the shared output part into every pipeline linked from it, so draws with another vertex layout read the wrong vertices. llvmpipe ignores the extra state, which is why CI passed.

Six Vulkan tests failed on NVIDIA from #216 on: render_equivalence_vulkan, render_equivalence_vulkan_remaining, enhanced_rendering_vulkan, sun_shadow_vulkan, sun_shadow_filter_reference_vulkan, probe_gpu_vulkan.

- Each part now gets only its own state (vertex input and assembly; viewport and rasteriser; depth and stencil; blend and samples) and null for the rest. Part sharing, fast linking and the prewarm workers are unchanged, so the speed-up stays.
- `vulkan_prewarm` gains a test: one program drawn with two vertex layouts, linked against whole pipelines. It fails on NVIDIA without the fix.
- #216's own linked-parts test now runs with prewar

merged.title: fix(rac2): Windows x64 crashes from calls typed in another argument order
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Going Commando ran on Linux and macOS but crashed on Windows: first in the title's menus, then in Aranos. Each crash was a call whose declared parameter order differs from the definition it reaches.

**Cause:** System V and AArch64, like the EE, pass integers and floats in separate registers, each kind in order. So `f(float, void *)` reaching `f(void *, float)` works there. On Windows x64 a position decides the register, so the callee reads a pointer from a float's bits. The crash addresses were float and colour bit patterns: `0x70FFFEED`, `0x0FDB0000`, `0x3EAC1242`.

Such a call can only come from three places. This covers each:

| Where | Crash | Change |
|---|---|---|
| The game's host C declaring game functions itself | `host/font.c` called FontPrintScaled (`func_0027F640`) as `(float, float, float, int, …)`: the title's text read through the colour | Declarations fixed; `abicheck --host` now compares them with `game_protos.h` and runs in `<id>_call_abi` |
| hostgen's call_copies r

merged.title: fix(hostgen): pass the hostgen tests with integer-only calls by kind
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Fixes the `port` CI job that #232 broke: 5 hostgen tests failed with `no thunk for 00110000`.

- **Test harness:** #232 sends every computed call with arguments through `openrac_guest_call_regs`. The harness's version exited when a function had no thunk, which is every function on POSIX, because the tests leave `OPENRAC_REGS_THUNKS` off. It now falls back to the all-registers cast, as `port/runtime/guest.cpp` does.
- **hostgen:** a cast of a named function, `((int (*)(int))f)(i)`, reaches a definition hostgen knows. It no longer counts as computed, so it keeps its `GFN` call through the definition's 64-bit result (`test_a_cast_to_an_int_result_keeps_the_64_bits`).

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest test_hostgen` on Ubuntu (WSL) with clang 18: 177 tests OK, none skipped.
- `openrac-rac2-ntsc.exe` regenerates and links on Windows; `ctest -R rac2-ntsc_call_abi` passes.
- Conventions check (clang-format 21.1.8): clean.
